objects.name: Chipkin Example B-LS
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID and the Object_Name with --deviceName (both at start-up; the heading shows the defaults). The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table, and Database_Revision, which the stack starts at 0 and increments as the objects are added at start-up: it reads 12 and stays 12, because nothing creates, deletes or renames an object afterwards (a command, a WriteGroup, a Schedule write, a time sync or a DeviceCommunicationControl changes no object). The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation and system status; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Chartreuse
objects.note: REAL setpoint; commandable via a 16-slot Priority_Array (WriteProperty/DS-WP-B); Present_Value, Priority_Array and Current_Command_Priority are resolved by the stack from the array the app maintains

objects.name: Jade
objects.note: REAL 0-100%; commandable via a 16-slot Priority_Array (WriteProperty/DS-WP-B) AND via the typed Lighting_Command SEQUENCE (DS-LO-B). The lighting engine is B-LD-CPP's (main.cpp section 1b): it runs every Table 12-67 operation over time - Present_Value is the target, Tracking_Value the level being driven, In_Progress fadeActive/rampActive while it moves, Egress_Active TRUE during a warn's egress time; NONE is refused. Jade is also Channel 1's local member, so a Channel write, a WriteGroup or Schedule 1 writes its Present_Value the same way. The dimming defaults and Egress_Time are writable, range-checked. Last_On_Value and Default_On_Value (100.0; required in 135-2024, cl. 12.54.44/45) are served by the app, Current_Command_Priority and Property_List by the stack.

objects.name: Garnet
objects.note: F-CHANNEL / F-EXTWRITE (canonical). BACnetChannelValue REAL, commandable via a 16-slot Priority_Array the application holds. At 64b2cfac5 every write to it (client WriteProperty, WriteGroup, the Schedule) reaches SetPropertyReal/SetPropertyNull on PRESENT_VALUE with a priority, not on PRIORITY_ARRAY with an index as BACnetStack_AddChannelObject's doc says, so both shapes are accepted (stack #3955, TODO.md). List_Of_Object_Property_References and Execution_Delay are stack-held, set with BACnetStack_AddObjectPropertyReferenceToChannel: one local reference to Lighting Output 1 (Jade), one remote reference to device 389016's Lighting Output 1. Every write to Present_Value - a matching WriteGroup (DS-WG-E-B), a WriteProperty or Schedule 1's write - is forwarded to both (cl. 12.53.5): Jade through the Set callbacks, device 389016 with a WriteProperty the stack sends through its Device_Address_Binding (proved by tests/channel_fanout_test.py). Write_Status is kept by the application from those writes' results (main.cpp section 2e): IDLE until the first write, IN_PROGRESS while a member's answer is outstanding, then SUCCESSFUL or FAILED (cl. 12.53.7) - FAILED after Schedule 1's start-up write, which is made before device 389016 is bound; a WriteProperty of Present_Value while IN_PROGRESS is refused with OBJECT / BUSY. Last_Priority starts at 16 (cl. 12.53.6).

objects.name: Saffron
objects.note: F-SCHED-E (canonical). Present_Value, Effective_Period and Priority_For_Writing are genuinely served - by the STACK's own Schedule engine, configured through the dedicated API (BACnetStack_AddScheduleObject, AddScheduleWeeklyTimeValue [09:00 on / 17:00 off daily], SetScheduleDefault, SetScheduleEffectivePeriod, SetSchedulePriorityForWriting [12]) rather than a GetProperty callback, which is what this generator's simple app/stack heuristic looks for; they are listed as accepted only because the generator has no third category for 'served by a dedicated stack API, not a callback'. AddScheduleObjectPropertyReference points the Schedule at Channel 1's Present_Value, written at Priority_For_Writing 12 (until v1.2.0 it named the Channel's Priority_Array, which a Channel does not have); one demo AddScheduleExceptionEventWithCalendarEntry covers today from 00:00:05, so it is in effect from start-up. Channel 1 forwards the Schedule's write to its members (cl. 12.53.5). Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal), the same pattern as Network Port's Reliability below.

objects.name: Cream
objects.note: F-SCHED-E support object. Present_Value ("is today in Date_List") is honestly always false: Date_List is a BACnetLIST of BACnetCalendarEntry (a variable-length list of a CHOICE type) and this stack build's customer surface has no Get callback shape that fits it (verified against CASBACnetStackDLL.h at the pin) - see TODO.md. Schedule 1's own exception-event scheduling does not depend on this: it uses the direct date/period form, AddScheduleExceptionEventWithCalendarEntry, confirmed functional in the stack's own doc comment (unlike AddScheduleExceptionEventWithCalendarReference, which the same doc comment says does not yet resolve a Calendar's Date_List - stack issue #963).

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)
